Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Atlas Insurance Group Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Atlas Insurance Group's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Underwriting Officer; David Chen, Chief Investment Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer; and Robert Kline, Chief Claims Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Atlas Insurance Group's performance for the third quarter. We delivered strong results, driven by favorable changes in actuarial assumptions netting out after offsets, a robust capital position with surplus growth, excellent policy retention rates across major lines, solid reinsurance recoveries both received and anticipated, disciplined combined ratio outlook, robust new business production volumes, and manageable catastrophe losses relative to gross written premiums. We are making significant progress on our digital transformation initiatives.

Michael, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Rivera: Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $520 million, or $2.45 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included strong premium growth, favorable reserve development, enhanced investment yields, reinsurance efficiencies, and cost discipline. Our combined ratio was 93.2%. Investment income for the quarter was $295 million. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with an RBC ratio of 445%. Our expense ratio also improved to 26.5%.

Let me expand on these results and the key aspects shaping our performance. First, on changes in actuarial assumptions and their impact—one of the primary drivers behind our reserve movements this quarter. These updates are grounded in the latest experience studies, peer benchmarking, and forward-looking scenario analysis using our stochastic CTE-95 models, applied under both US GAAP LDTI for long-duration targeted improvements and IFRS 17 for our international operations. The net impact was a $285 million after-tax charge to earnings, about 8% of our adjusted operating income, split roughly 60/40 between life and annuity reserves versus property-casualty lines. Favorable releases in health and group life provided some offset, but year-to-date, these changes have cumulatively affected earnings by $420 million. We're guiding for stability in 2025 as we lap prior updates and interest rates potentially level off.

On the longevity and mortality front for our $180 billion fixed indexed annuity and whole life blocks, we incorporated the 2023 Society of Actuaries' LP-2022 scale, reflecting post-COVID normalization. We've adjusted improvement rates to 1.2% per annum for ages 65+, aligning with CMI UK data and our own studies across 2.5 million policyholders, accounting for long COVID effects and deferred surgeries. This led to a $210 million reserve strengthening, lifting life reserves by 1.4% and boosting our RBC ratio by 20 basis points to 445%, while mirroring peers like Allianz and AXA under Solvency II.

Discount rates were lowered from 3.1% to 2.8% for LDTI cohorts, with the Fed's terminal rate at 4.75-5%, impacting our $120 billion liability portfolio with a $95 million charge due to higher present values. In P&C cat reserves, we saw a $25 million favorable release post-Hurricane Ian data, with quarterly stress-testing showing $150 million sensitivity per 50 basis point shift.

Lapse and surrender rates rose in variable annuities, up 15% with economic recovery, revising non-economic lapses to 5.2% annually for early years based on IRS data and peers like Prudential and Athene—a $65 million hit. Morbidity assumptions in our $40 billion Medicare Advantage and stop-loss improved favorably by $40 million from telehealth and obesity trends, with group life persistency at 88% via wellness programs.

Regionally, the US (75% of reserves) saw longevity and discount pressures but a $15 million cat frequency benefit in Florida from Swiss Re and Munich Re terms. Europe (15%) had slight IFRS 17 CSM acceleration with a €30 million drag, mitigated by Rothesay Life reinsurance. Asia-Pacific (10%) gained $20 million from Japanese long-term care morbidity but faced Hong Kong UL lapses, with PartnerRe swaps in pilot.

We've invested $50 million in AI-driven assumption governance with Milliman's platform, cutting update cycles to three weeks and benchmarking against 50 carriers. Climate modeling upped California wildfire assumptions 10%, and inflation at 3.2% raised expense scaling 2%, fitting our 92% combined outlook. Strategically, $500 million in macro hedges caps volatility at under 5% of EPS, shifting to dynamic FIA products for 12% ROE uplift by 2026, with RenaissanceRe quota-share and RGA longevity covers, plus NAIC PBR adoption smoothing earnings. Our core underwriting stays at 91.5% combined.

Turning to our capital position and statutory surplus levels, which underpin our financial strength. We closed Q3 with statutory surplus of $13.2 billion, up 10.5% year-over-year from $11.95 billion. This is our 16th year of growth despite cats like Idalia analogs and wildfires totaling $900 million pre-tax in P&C.

Our consolidated RBC ratio is 445%, above the 200% company action level and our 400% target, up from 410% last year and ahead of peers like Travelers at 380% and Chubb at 410%. Drivers include $1.5 billion in statutory operating income, with $1 billion from P&C at 92.5% combined, retaining $700 million post $480 million dividend (up 9%) and $350 million buybacks.

Investments yielded 4.3% on our $47 billion portfolio, with $450 million unrealized gains; allocation is 65% fixed income (AA- average), 20% equities, 15% alternatives, duration 5.3 years. Optimization via $550 million Swiss Re quota-share on homeowners freed $200 million capital, plus $450 million cat bonds at 6.7% coupon.

US ops (72% surplus, $9.5 billion) at 460% RBC with 8% premium growth; Europe (15%, $2 billion) at 225% Solvency II via telematics; Asia-Pacific (13%, $1.7 billion) up 20% on life/health.

For 2025, expect 9-11% surplus growth assuming normalized cats (1-in-100 PML $2.2 billion, 3.6x covered). Priorities: $2.2 billion for M&A in cyber, $550 million digital platforms with RMS/AIR; 11% dividend to $4.95/share, $550 million buybacks; ORSA stresses pass with buffers.

Next, policy retention rates by major product line—a testament to our underwriting discipline and service. Overall book retention was 91.5%, up 130 basis points YoY and 50 bps sequentially, 13th straight quarter improving, topping peers like Progressive's 89% personal or Travelers' 92% commercial.

Personal lines at 88.8% (+160 bps YoY): Auto 87.5% with HorizonDrive telematics at 36% penetration for 16% better retention; homeowners 90.4% via 63% bundling (96% retained). California at 86% on cats/reg caps, Texas/Florida 90-91%.

Commercial P&C at 93.7% (+90 bps): Middle-market 94.5% via AI risk assessment cutting cancellations 20%; workers' comp 95.4% with SafetyNet (-10% frequency). Large accounts 92.5%, UK 91.5%, Australia 94.5% on cyber hybrids.

Group life/health at 97.1% (+60 bps): Voluntary 97.8%, HealthChoice 96.5% with 48-hour digital claims; NA 97.8%, Europe 95.8%.

Specialty at 92.4% (+130 bps): Cyber 92.1% via threat monitoring, D&O 93.8%, marine 90.5% with parametrics (96% cargo).

Pillars: myAtlas app 80% adoption (+23% retention), 8.5% premium growth discipline, 1.3 products/household (+9 points). US 92.8%, Europe 90.1%, EM 88.5% (+220 bps). Q4 guide 92.2%, with $160M tech including GenAI for 3-point LoyaltyLock uplift. Our moat vs. insurtechs targets 93%+ by 2025.

On reinsurance recoveries received and expected—a standout for P&C. YTD gross losses $1.3 billion (wildfires $480M, windstorms $350M, floods $270M), net $720M (44% net-to-gross). Received $420 million YTD, 25% YoY up, 86% efficiency on $490M billable; 72% within 90 days.

Property cat $290M (82% collected, Woolsey extension $125M Munich/PartnerRe, Ciarán $95M); casualty $115M (93%); retro $35M ILS.

Expected $190-230M more (total 51-54% recovery), point $210M ($125M Q4). IBNR/case $145M (wildfires $85M RMS v18.1), reinstatements $45M (110% priced), disputes $15M upside.

Trends: 52% recovery vs. 42% 2022, AI claims/Verisk reducing disputes 32%. NA 58% expected ($122M), Europe 27% ($57M Hannover parametric), APAC 15% ($32M Korean Re).

Program $2.9B (13% up): 16% ILS ($325M Atlas Shield 4.6% coupon savings), AIR Touchstone, ReinsureAI (42% faster billing). Leverage 2.7x supports 94.5% combined target, excess for cyber M&A like $160M flood buy.

Combined ratio guidance: Q4 92-95% (5-8% margin), FY2025 93-96%, below Travelers 94.8%/Progressive 92.5%.

Loss/LAE 66-69% Q4, 67-70% FY: 2.5 pts PYD (auto/wc inflation 4.5%), cats $275-375M Q4 (1.6-2.1 pts, FY $1.3-1.6B 1-in-10), 7.5% earned growth/10% high-hazard rates.

Expense 26-27% (60 bps better): AI triage 29% faster/16 bps save (EU motor next), commissions 12.4% direct shift, RPA 42% admin.

US ex-cat 90.5-93.5% (UBI 37%), Europe 95.5-98.5% (German 13% pricing), APAC 92.5-95.5%. Fortress framework: GLMs, <14% long-tail, $550M repurchases, parametric pilots (1 pt cat shave). Buffers vs. inflation/re costs/macro.

New business production: Q3 APE $2.95B (+20% YoY, 8% seq), 1.25M policies (+24%). Life/annuities $1.62B (56%, +27%, IUL/term crediting 5.3-5.9%, FIA $880M +34%, 360k policies bancassurance 30%). P&C $1.03B (35%, +14%, 775k policies, cyber/D&O +24%, auto/home 9% UBI 44%). Health/specialty $300M (10%, +16%, 115k, parametrics).

NA 73% $2.15B (+22%), Europe 17.5% $516M (+13%), APAC 9.5% $280M (+17%). Avg premium $2,450 (+15%), 33% conversion GenAI quotes. Initiatives: ApexConnect 42% P&C, Munich XL unlocking $475M, $260M health M&A. NBV margin 29%, CSM $1.15B annual. FY2024 $11.3-11.8B (+18-22%).

Finally, total catastrophe losses: Q3 $1.5B pre-tax (+30% YoY), 14.5% of $10.35B GWP (vs. 11% prior), YTD $3.35B/10.9% $30.7B GWP (vs. 9% prior), net $900M recoveries.

US hurricanes 57% $855M (Gulf Cat4 $475M PML), Europe secondary 24% $360M (Rhine/Italy), APAC 19% $285M (fires/typhoon). Ex-cat combined 92.4%, underlying 98.5% best-in-class.

Trends per Swiss Re sigma $115B global (+22%), inflation 16%; trimmed SE US 9%, parametrics 16%, 2025 tower +27% clash Lloyd's. Verisk/Touchstone to 2050 (+32% severity), 7.5% rates/9.5% earned growth. Resilience cyber hybrids/ILS 13%, Q4 $650-850M/6.5-8.5% GWP.

These elements position us strongly.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Michael. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our commercial P&C line. We are actively managing our exposure to secondary perils and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including AI-integrated cat modeling and telematics for auto.

David Chen: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in fixed income and alternatives, yielding steady income amid rate stability.

Robert Kline: I'd like to briefly address our claims performance. We've implemented several initiatives to streamline our claims process and improve customer satisfaction, including AI triage and digital portals. We are seeing positive results in terms of reduced claims processing times, down 30% on average.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the reserve development trends excluding the actuarial updates?

Johnathan Hale: Good morning, Alex. Yes, ex-actuarial changes, prior year development was favorable by $120 million, mainly in commercial auto and workers' comp where severity came in better than expected due to moderated medical inflation. This contributed about 1.2 points to the combined ratio improvement.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jamie Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Jamie Patel: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of recent interest rate movements on your business?

Michael Rivera: Good morning, Jamie. Rate compression at the long end has increased liability present values under LDTI by $95 million as noted, but our hedges—$500 million in swaps—have contained the earnings volatility. On the asset side, our portfolio yield held at 4.3%, and we're positioned for stability if rates peak.

Operator: Our next question comes from Chris Wong with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Chris Wong: What is the expected impact of upcoming regulatory changes like expanded PBR adoption on your underwriting strategy?

Elena Vasquez: Good morning, Chris. PBR full adoption next year will smooth earnings by aligning reserves more dynamically with experience, allowing us to optimize capital in life lines. We're already compliant in pilots, and it supports our shift to higher-margin FIA and cyber without increasing tail risks.

Operator: Our next question comes from Taylor Brooks with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Taylor Brooks: Thanks. On new business, how sustainable is the APE growth given softening re-pricing?

Michael Rivera: Good morning, Taylor. Very sustainable—our 20% YoY reflects 7% earned rate gains and 33% digital conversion, with reinsurance optimization unlocking appetite. FY guide holds at 18-22% even with stable cats under $1.3 billion.

Operator: Our final question today from Dana Lee with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Dana Lee: Good morning. Can you elaborate on cat load expectations for Q4?

Elena Vasquez: Good morning, Dana. Q4 cats guided at $650-850 million or 6.5-8.5% GWP, normalized secondary activity post-peak season. Our parametrics and refreshed tower limit net to 40%, supporting ex-cat 92-93%.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Atlas Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
